sub_graphs.title: Blob Encoding and Cell Production Lifecycle
sub_graphs.description: Models the full pipeline from raw blob data through polynomial conversion, Reed-Solomon extension, and cell/proof generation

nodes.label: Raw Blob Received
nodes.description: A raw blob of BYTES_PER_BLOB bytes has been provided as input for encoding

nodes.label: Validate Blob Length
nodes.description: Check that len(blob) == BYTES_PER_BLOB; reject if invalid

nodes.label: Convert Blob to Polynomial
nodes.description: Convert raw blob bytes into evaluation-form polynomial via blob_to_polynomial()

nodes.label: Convert Evaluation to Coefficient Form
nodes.description: Apply bit-reversal permutation and inverse FFT to transform evaluation-form polynomial to coefficient form over FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB roots of unity

nodes.label: Polynomial in Coefficient Form
nodes.description: Polynomial is now in coefficient representation, ready for extension and cell computation

nodes.label: Compute All Cells and KZG Proofs
nodes.description: For each cell index 0..CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB: evaluate polynomial over the cell's coset and compute KZG multi-proof via quotient polynomial commitment

nodes.label: All Cells and Proofs Generated
nodes.description: CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB cells and corresponding KZG proofs have been produced, ready for distribution

sub_graphs.title: Cell KZG Proof Batch Verification
sub_graphs.description: Models the batch verification of cell KZG proofs using Fiat-Shamir challenge and pairing checks

nodes.label: Cells and Proofs Received for Verification
nodes.description: A batch of cells, proofs, commitments, and cell indices has been received for verification

nodes.label: Validate Batch Input Lengths and Formats
nodes.description: Check: all sequences equal length, each commitment is BYTES_PER_COMMITMENT, each proof is BYTES_PER_PROOF, each cell is BYTES_PER_CELL, each cell_index < CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB

nodes.label: Deserialize Commitments and Proofs
nodes.description: Convert bytes to BLS group elements via bytes_to_kzg_commitment() and bytes_to_kzg_proof(); deduplicate commitments

nodes.label: Convert Cells to Coset Evaluations
nodes.description: For each cell, convert untrusted byte data to field elements via cell_to_coset_evals(), which uses bytes_to_bls_field() per element

nodes.label: Compute Fiat-Shamir Challenge
nodes.description: Hash domain separator, blob/cell parameters, all commitments, cell indices, evaluations, and proofs to produce deterministic random challenge r

nodes.label: Compute Pairing Check Arguments
nodes.description: Compute LL = sum(r^k * proofs[k]), weights per commitment, RLC = sum(weights[i]*commitments[i]), RLI via Lagrange interpolation on cosets, RLP with coset shifts; combine into RL = RLC - RLI + RLP

nodes.label: Execute BLS Pairing Check
nodes.description: Verify pairing equation: e(LL, [s^n]) == e(RL, [1]) using KZG_SETUP_G2_MONOMIAL[FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_CELL]

nodes.label: Batch Verification Result
nodes.description: Pairing check returns true (all cells valid) or false (at least one cell invalid)

edges.label: Cells, proofs, commitments submitted for verification
Begin input validation
Inputs valid, deserialize BLS elements
Convert cell bytes to field elements
Compute deterministic random challenge from all inputs
Use challenge r to build linear combination for pairing
Execute final pairing verification
Return boolean verification result

external_entities.name: Cell Provider (Peer Node)
external_entities.description: External peer or network source providing cells, proofs, and commitments for verification - untrusted input

sub_graphs.title: Cell Recovery via Reed-Solomon Reconstruction
sub_graphs.description: Models the data recovery process when some cells are missing, using polynomial interpolation over remaining cells with a 50% minimum threshold

nodes.label: Partial Cell Set Received
nodes.description: A subset of cells (at least 50%) with their indices has been provided for recovery

nodes.label: Validate Recovery Inputs
nodes.description: Check: len(cell_indices) == len(cells), CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB/2 <= count <= CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB, no duplicates, ascending order, all indices < CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB, each cell length == BYTES_PER_CELL

nodes.label: Identify Missing Cell Indices
nodes.description: Compute the set of cell indices not present in the provided partial set

nodes.label: Construct Vanishing Polynomial
nodes.description: Build polynomial Z(x) that vanishes at all evaluation points of missing cells; uses small-domain roots then extends via sparse coefficient placement every FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_CELL positions

nodes.label: Multiply Extended Evaluations by Vanishing Polynomial
nodes.description: Flatten known coset evaluations (zero-fill missing) in bit-reversal order, convert Z(x) to evaluation form via FFT, pointwise multiply E(x)*Z(x)

nodes.label: Recover Polynomial via Coset Division
nodes.description: Inverse FFT to get (P*Z)(x) coefficients, evaluate both (P*Z)(x) and Z(x) over a coset, divide pointwise, inverse coset FFT to recover P(x) coefficients

nodes.label: Full Polynomial Recovered
nodes.description: The first FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB coefficients of the original polynomial have been reconstructed

nodes.label: Recompute All Cells and Proofs
nodes.description: Using recovered polynomial, recompute all CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB cells and KZG proofs from scratch

nodes.label: All Cells and Proofs Recovered
nodes.description: Complete set of cells and proofs has been reconstructed from the partial input

edges.label: Partial cell set provided for recovery
Validate recovery preconditions
Inputs valid, identify missing indices
Build vanishing polynomial for missing cell cosets
edges.condition: Build vanishing polynomial for missing cell cosets

edges.label: Multiply evaluations by vanishing polynomial in evaluation domain
Divide out vanishing polynomial via coset FFT
Original polynomial coefficients recovered
Recompute all cells and proofs from recovered polynomial
All cells and proofs reconstructed

sub_graphs.title: Trust Boundaries in Cell Processing
sub_graphs.description: Models the trust boundaries where untrusted external data (cells, proofs, commitments) enters the cryptographic verification pipeline

nodes.label: Untrusted Bytes Received
nodes.description: Raw bytes for commitments, proofs, cells, and indices received from an untrusted external source

nodes.label: Validate Byte Lengths
nodes.description: Check each commitment is BYTES_PER_COMMITMENT, each proof is BYTES_PER_PROOF, each cell is BYTES_PER_CELL

nodes.label: Validate Cell Index Bounds
nodes.description: Check all cell_indices < CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB to prevent out-of-bounds access to root-of-unity tables

nodes.label: Deserialize BLS Group Elements
nodes.description: Convert raw bytes to BLS12-381 group elements; bytes_to_kzg_commitment() and bytes_to_kzg_proof() perform subgroup checks

nodes.label: Convert Cell Bytes to Field Elements
nodes.description: cell_to_coset_evals() converts each BYTES_PER_FIELD_ELEMENT chunk via bytes_to_bls_field(); validates each value < BLS_MODULUS

nodes.label: Trusted Cryptographic Elements Ready
nodes.description: All inputs have been validated and deserialized into trusted BLS field/group elements safe for cryptographic operations

Check index bounds

external_entities.name: Network Peer
external_entities.description: Untrusted peer node providing cells, proofs, and commitments over the P2P network

ambiguities.text: The cell_to_coset_evals function converts 'untrusted' Cell bytes to 'trusted' CosetEvals, but the spec does not explicitly define what makes bytes_to_bls_field() a trust boundary (e.g., whether it checks < BLS_MODULUS or rejects invalid encodings).
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume bytes_to_bls_field() validates that the integer representation is < BLS_MODULUS and raises an error otherwise. This is the standard BLS field deserialization behavior.

ambiguities.text: The spec does not specify behavior when polynomial multiplication in multiply_polynomialcoeff results in a polynomial exceeding FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_EXT_BLOB coefficients, only asserting len(a)+len(b)-1 <= FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_EXT_BLOB.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume the assertion is a hard precondition and callers must ensure it holds. Violation indicates a programming error, not a runtime condition to handle gracefully.

ambiguities.text: The recovery function requires cell_indices to be 'in ascending order' but does not specify whether this is a strict requirement or an optimization hint.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume this is a strict precondition enforced by the implementation. Non-ascending indices should cause the function to fail.

ambiguities.text: The Fiat-Shamir challenge computation hashes 'all commitments' but commitment deduplication happens before this step. It is unclear whether the hash is computed over the original (with duplicates) or deduplicated commitment list.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume the hash is computed over the original input (including duplicates), as the challenge must be deterministic based on the exact inputs provided by the caller.

implicit_assumptions.description: The KZG trusted setup (KZG_SETUP_G1_MONOMIAL, KZG_SETUP_G2_MONOMIAL) was generated correctly and the toxic waste was destroyed.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: An attacker with the toxic waste could forge valid KZG proofs for arbitrary polynomial evaluations, completely breaking data availability guarantees.

implicit_assumptions.description: An attacker cannot solve the discrete logarithm problem on BLS12-381 or break the polynomial commitment binding property.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Attacker could create cells with valid proofs that do not correspond to the committed blob, enabling data withholding attacks.

implicit_assumptions.description: The Fiat-Shamir heuristic (hashing all inputs to produce challenge r) produces a sufficiently random challenge in the random oracle model.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: An attacker could craft inputs that produce a predictable challenge value, potentially allowing invalid cell batches to pass verification.

implicit_assumptions.description: At least 50% of cells (CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB / 2) are available for recovery to succeed, relying on the Reed-Solomon 2x extension factor.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Data recovery would fail silently or produce incorrect results if fewer than 50% of cells are available, leading to data unavailability.

implicit_assumptions.description: PRIMITIVE_ROOT_OF_UNITY is a valid generator of the multiplicative subgroup of the required order in the BLS12-381 scalar field.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: FFT computations would produce incorrect results, leading to invalid cell encodings and failed verifications across the entire system.
